1m211a6:265: Azerbaijani is morphologically rich: words encode grammatical meaning through suffixes, so standard English-optimized tokenizers split them into many subword fragments. BBPE (Byte-Level Byte-Pair Encoding) starts from raw bytes rather than a predefined character set and iteratively merges the most frequent byte pairs, fully covering Azerbaijani's special characters. We experimented with vocab sizes from 50k to 100k, finally choosing 100k. Evaluation used BPB (Bits-Per-Byte) rather than perplexity, because BPB normalizes at the byte level to remove vocabulary-size effects: the custom tokenizer achieved BPB 0.5795 vs. baseline 0.6830, proving that the efficiency gain did not sacrifice modeling quality.

1og9rrj:268: After CPT, the model can fluently predict Azerbaijani tokens but lacks the concept of conversational structure. LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and injects low-rank decomposition matrices into the attention layers (q/k/v/o projections and gate/up/down projections), reducing trainable parameters to a small fraction of the total. Configuration: rank=64, alpha=28, dropout=0.05, max_seq_len=1024. It completes in minutes on a single ml.g5.8xlarge (A10G) GPU, using a Llama-style chat template with assistant-only loss masking that penalizes only assistant response tokens and EOT tokens.

1s4av5g:169: FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel) evenly shards model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across all GPUs, enabling large-model training beyond single-GPU memory limits. Liger Kernel provides fused RMSNorm and RoPE implementations that reduce inter-GPU communication and memory fragmentation. The combination is the best practice for small and medium teams training LLMs on SageMaker.

61b2ye:152: Azerbaijani (~30 million native speakers) is a low-resource language. With insufficient training data, traditional BPE tokenizers produce many fragment tokens, inflating sequence lengths and reducing training efficiency. BBPE (Byte-Level BPE) avoids the subword fragmentation problem by operating at the byte level, at the cost of a larger vocabulary and slightly slower inference. This trade-off exists in all low-resource LLM training.
6ndem5:53: LoRA fine-tuning: completes in minutes on a single A10G GPU, rank=64, alpha=28, dropout=0.05.
cq3ktx:306: The main bottleneck during continued pretraining (CPT) is GPU memory: with DDP on ml.p4d.24xlarge, the maximum batch_size per GPU is 2; after FSDP shards parameters/gradients/optimizer states, model state per GPU drops to 1.17 GB (from 9.23 GB), enabling batch_size up to 14. Liger Kernels are LinkedIn's open-source Triton-based fused kernels that fuse multiple layers into a single GPU kernel launch, further reducing intermediate memory allocation. On ml.p5.48xlarge, peak memory dropped from 64GB to 27GB (-58%), and per-GPU throughput rose from 63,771 to 78,319 tokens/s (+23%).

rk3ooz:213: Training LLMs for low-resource, morphologically complex languages (e.g., Azerbaijani) requires solving three interdependent bottlenecks: encoding efficiency (a custom BBPE tokenizer reduces fertility from 3.22 to 1.59 tokens/word), GPU memory utilization (FSDP shards gradients/optimizer states, Liger Kernel fuses operators to reduce intermediate memory allocation), and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (two-phase CPT + LoRA). The three-stage pipeline tokenizer→CPT→LoRA is reusable for any low-resource language.
